correctness.rationale: In a complete multipartite graph, every vertex of part \(V_i\) has exactly \(s-s_i\) neighbors in \(S\), so total \(k\)-tuple domination is equivalent to \(s-s_i\ge k\). If the part is not full, an omitted vertex has exactly \(N-s-n_i+s_i\) neighbors in the complement, giving the second condition. For fixed \(s\), the allowed non-full values are precisely the stated interval \([L_i(s),U_i(s)]\), while the full value \(n_i\) is allowed exactly when it satisfies total domination. Independent binomial choices by part and coefficient extraction at total degree \(s\) therefore give the enumerator exactly.

originality.rationale: Kazemi's complete-multipartite proof already writes the two decisive arbitrary-set inequalities in substance: for an arbitrary k-tuple total restrained dominating set \(S\), every part satisfies \(\sum_j s_j-s_i\ge k\), and every omitted vertex in an incomplete part is required to have at least \(k\) neighbors among the omitted vertices in the other incomplete parts. These are exactly the submitted profile conditions after notation is expanded. The displayed generating function is then a routine coefficient-packaging of those already established independent partwise bounds with binomial multiplicities. Under implication-level originality, the absence of an explicit published polynomial does not make this a new mathematical claim.
